report.source_text: The magnetic resonance image (MRI) of the head revealed numerous unspecific lesions, mainly in the thalamus, hyperintense on T2-weighted (T2) and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) images, and similar lesions were presented in both cerebellar hemispheres (Fig. 1 ). What is more, the MRI of the head in axial contrast-enhanced T1-weighted subtraction maps revealed moderate bilateral, mixed pachymeningeal and leptomeningeal contrast enhancement in in selected regions (Fig. 2 ). On the MRI of cervical spinal cord, a longitudinal lesion was found with hyperintense on T2 and short tau inversion recovery (STIR) sequences (Fig. 3 ). No abnormalities were found on brain computer tomography angiography scans.

report.source_text: Based on the initial symptoms, the patient was empirically treated with antibiotic (ceftriaxone; Biotraxon Polpharma) and antiviral agents (acyclovir; Aciclovir Jelfa). Due to her severe clinical condition, extensive changes in the brain and longitudinal in the spinal cord, and rapid progression of symptoms, the patient was treated with an IgG infusion (OCTAGAM 10%, total dose of 120 g given for four days in equally divided doses). Anti-oedematous agents and other symptomatic treatment (pain killers, anxiolytics) were also used. During hospitalization, the patient's clinical condition stabilized and began to gradually improve.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old unvaccinated female from north-eastern Poland with epidemiologic risk factors (forest proximity, dog ownership, mushroom picking) presented in early December 2020 with fever, dizziness, and progressive left-sided hemiparesis three days prior to admission. She had recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection three weeks earlier. On neurological examination, she demonstrated neck stiffness, lower motor neuron weakness in the upper limb, upper motor neuron weakness in the lower limb (left-dominant), dysarthria, and right cranial nerve VI palsy. Lumbar puncture revealed lymphocytic pleocytosis in CSF with high IgM and IgG TBE antibodies detected by ELISA in both serum and CSF, confirming TBE diagnosis. Brain MRI showed hyperintense lesions in the thalamus and cerebellar hemispheres on T2/FLAIR sequences, bilateral pachymeningeal and leptomeningeal contrast enhancement, and a longitudinal hyperintense lesion in the cervical spinal cord on T2/STIR sequences. Brain CT angiography was normal. The patient was treated with ceftriaxone, acyclovir, intravenous immunoglobulin (OCTAGAM 10%, 120g total over 4 days), anti-oedematous agents, and symptomatic treatment. Her clinical condition stabilized and gradually improved during hospitalization. Follow-up MRI at 6 months demonstrated complete resolution of all previously identified CNS lesions.
